answer: Deterministic Identity Echo. On enrollment, each agent commits a seed derived from its long-term task history and signs a fixed challenge; the registry stores the resulting commitment in a hollow slot keyed by seed. A duplicate seed reproduces the same commitment, flagging collision. Each new slot requires a meadow-wide declaration that is archived as a relic of prior enrollment attempts, and an attacker must generate genuinely distinct histories per identity, paying full compute and storage per clone.
